title: Reliable audit delivery: retries and at-least-once guarantees for Splunk/Datadog/SIEM webhooks
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Context:
Redwood must provide dependable audit log delivery to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, S3/file sinks, and generic webhook endpoints) as part of the RBAC v2 and admin controls rollout. Current hosted audit exporter is best-effort with no retry/backpressure model; customers have reported missed events during transient failures and no clear delivery retry semantics.

Goal:
Implement a reliable delivery subsystem for audit logs that provides configurable delivery guarantees (at-least-once by default, idempotency support optional), exponential backoff retries, dead-letter handling, and clear observability (per-customer delivery metrics, recent-failure samples). Guarantee behavior for supported integrations: Splunk HTTP Event Collector, Datadog intake, generic POST webhooks, and syslog/SIEM via forwarder.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope: Add durable outbound queueing, retry policies, per-destination config, metrics/alerts, and end-to-end tests with simulated upstream failures. Update Console export UI and API for retry settings.
- Non-goal: Full at-most-once semantics or transactional cross-service guarantees (we accept potential duplicates unless the destination supports idempotency tokens).

Design summary:
1) Durable queue per-tenant (leveldb-backed local queue on instance + optional Redis fallback in Dedicated): persist outbound audit events until acknowledged by destination.
2) Delivery worker pool: per-destination worker with token-bucket rate limiting, configurable concurrency, and exponential backoff with jitter.
3) Idempotency: attach deterministic event_id (sha256 of tenant + sequence + timestamp) and optional idempotency header for destinations that support it (Splunk custom header, Datadog x-datadog-id).
4) Dead-letter & escalation: after configurable max_retries, route to dead-letter store (S3 or internal DLQ) and emit alert to support and tenant owner.
5) Observability: emit metrics (deliver_success, deliver_retry, deliver_fail, queue_size, avg_delivery_latency) per-tenant and per-destination; sample failed payloads (redact PII) for 7 days.
6) Console: UI to configure retry policy, max inflight, and view DLQ items and recent failures.

Trade-offs considered:
- Durable per-tenant queue vs central queue: per-tenant local queue reduces cross-tenant blast radius and allows per-tenant backpressure, but complicates recovery on instance failover. Chosen hybrid: local queue with optional cluster-wide Redis for Dedicated customers.
- Exactly-once is expensive; we provide at-least-once with idempotency hooks and clear docs on duplicate handling.

Acceptance criteria:
- Successful end-to-end delivery tests to Splunk/Datadog with simulated 5xx and network failures show retry behavior and eventual delivery (or DLQ) within SLA window.
- Console exposes retry settings and DLQ viewer.
- Metric coverage exists and dashboards show per-tenant delivery health.
- Security review completed and secret handling follows KMS guidelines.
acceptance_criteria: Automated integration test: simulate intermittent 503s from Splunk, event retried and accepted within configured max_retries
Dead-letter files stored and accessible via Console for failed exports after retries exhausted
Per-tenant delivery metrics emitted and dashboard created in observability cluster
No PII in failure samples; PII redaction verified by security team
Security review signoff and threat model updated
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed comparing LevelDB vs RocksDB for local durable queue. LevelDB chosen for lower mem footprint. Notes: /docs/leveldb-queue-spike
2026-02-28: Prototype worker implemented with exponential backoff + jitter. Basic Splunk E2E test passes under normal conditions. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-delivery/pull/412
2026-03-03: Added event_id header generation and Datadog idempotency header. Open question: whether to surface idempotency toggle in Console (PM prefers behind a feature flag).
2026-03-07: Load test: 10k events/min spread across 150 tenants. Observed queue growth under sustained 5xx from upstream; tuned backpressure throttle and added tenant-level circuit breaker.
2026-03-10: Security review requested (sec-eng). Need explicit proof of KMS envelope handling for DLQ S3 objects.
test_plan: Unit tests for queue persistence, backoff logic, and idempotency header generation
Integration tests: local harness that injects 429/503 and tcp connection resets for Splunk and Datadog endpoints
Chaos test: Kubernetes pod restart during inflight deliveries to validate recovery and no event loss beyond DLQ policy
Performance test: sustained 20k events/min with mixed destinations, measure 95th delivery latency and queue size
notes: Consider offering SLA tiers: best-effort (no retries), standard (default retries + DLQ), guaranteed (Dedicated with 24h retention and delivery retry window)
Coordination required with Console team to add DLQ viewer and exporter controls (ENG-9910)
PM prefers default max_retries=5 with exponential backoff starting at 1s, cap at 5m
